summary.whatItDoes: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) is an MCP server and CLI that lets a coding agent inspect native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies and websites without their source code, returning findings together with the evidence and limitations behind them.
intendedUsers: Developers who use coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Gemini CLI
People curious how a feature in an existing app is implemented
learningOpportunities: Study how an MCP server exposes analysis tools to an agent and returns evidence with each result.
Learn what static analysis of an Electron app reveals: modules, imports and Electron boundaries.
Compare agent-driven workflows with running the same commands from a terminal.

smallExperiment.title: Statically inspect an Electron app you own
steps: Read the Quick start and the CLI and Evidence guide in the repository first.
Inside a disposable VM or container with Node.js 22+, extract an Electron app you built yourself.
Run the documented analyze-javascript-application command with --json against that directory.
Review the modules, imports and Electron boundaries it reports against what you know of your app.

caveats: Setup changes your agent configuration; the README asks you to review the proposed changes before approving them.
Native analysis depends on Hopper, Ghidra or IDA being installed, and support varies by target and host.
Only analyse software you are licensed and permitted to reverse engineer.
The README notes that REA changes quickly, so commands may differ between releases.
